tagline: Up the Payette, from the whitewater to the lake.
intro: Out of Eagle the road climbs over Spring Valley Summit and drops 1,600 feet down Horseshoe Bend Hill to the Payette River, at a town named for the U-turn the river makes there. From there it goes up the river. Past Banks it takes the North Fork, crosses it on the Rainbow Bridge of 1933, and climbs into Round Valley.

Long Valley comes next, the road running along the east shore of Cascade Reservoir, and then McCall on the south shore of Payette Lake. West of town the highway tops out at 5,324 feet on Goose Creek Summit and goes down a narrow, twisty canyon to New Meadows.

moments.title: Banks
moments.text: The North and South forks of the Payette meet here, and the whitewater run called the Main starts at Banks and keeps company with the highway down to Horseshoe Bend.

moments.title: Smiths Ferry
moments.text: Where the North Fork briefly calms and widens, a ferry took livestock across to summer pasture from 1887, and in 1891 it was sold to a Jim Smith, whose name stuck.

moments.title: McCall
moments.text: Hollywood filmed Northwest Passage here in 1938, Idaho woods standing in for New England, and Payette Lake is said to keep a sea serpent, named Sharlie in 1954.
